claim: Five levels = five questions: L1 "Find it by an exact word or name?" | L2 "Pull everything on a certain topic together?" | L3 "I searched different words than I wrote?" | L4 "Trace relationship chains across a cast? (CRM)" | L5 "Consolidate on its own while I'm away?". Complexity climbs as you go up, not cost. Most people land at 1-3.
Two jobs, one that matters: Saving (Notes IN — everyone obsesses here) vs Finding (Notes OUT — where it falls apart). The ladder measures one thing: can you find it again?

LEVEL 1 · NO TERMINAL · FREE TO SET UP — 'The Folder + CLAUDE.md'. Question: 'Find it by an exact word, name, or filename?'. Why you need it: stop re-explaining your setup, ask in English it searches, free a few tokens per ask. The wall: only finds exact words, grows too big -> ignored. Your move: one folder + a 20-line CLAUDE.md about you. Most people stop here.

LEVEL 2 · NO TERMINAL · A FEW DOLLARS OF TOKENS TO BUILD — 'The Curated Wiki'. Question: 'Pull everything on a topic together, and build on it?'. Why: 30+ notes you forget what's in them, index page + summaries + links, Claude builds on past research. Wall: you must keep feeding it, a wrong summary loads as if true. Move: ask Claude for an index + one-line summaries, then cross-link. The structure is the level. A Zettelkasten is just this by hand.

Testo integrale vector-index/how-search-works.md: 5 concetti in versione semplice - Chunking (note lunghe spezzate per heading/paragrafo prima dell'embedding, la qualita' dei chunk conta piu' del modello scelto), Embedding (ogni chunk diventa un vettore/fingerprint numerico), Search (la domanda diventa vettore, vincono i vettori piu' vicini), Hybrid (meaning-search + keyword-search insieme per non perdere match esatti), Re-ranking (upgrade reale successivo: un piccolo re-ranker rilegge la domanda contro ogni risultato per precisione, piu' economico e ad alto ROI del knowledge graph). LEVEL 4 · TERMINAL + REAL WORK · FREE SOFTWARE, CHEAP TO RUN — 'Knowledge Graph: usually the skip rung'. Question: 'Are my questions relationship chains across a recurring cast? (CRM)'. Disegno SKIP per prosa/decision notes (quasi tutti) vs disegno 'recurring cast' con edge tipizzato endorsed_by. Perche' saltarlo: le domande non sono catene di relazioni, costa poco farlo girare ma l'effort non verra' usato. Quando E' il tuo livello: le domande incatenano un cast ricorrente (VC, recruiter, BD) -> allora costruiscilo (LightRAG).

LEVEL 5 · TERMINAL + YOU RUN A SERVER · REAL BURDEN — 'Always-on Brain-OS (gbrain)'. Question: 'Consolidate on its own while I'm away?'. Cosa lo rende diverso: unico livello che lavora mentre dormi, 'nightly dream cycle' arricchisce le note. Il muro: real burden (server 24/7), per Q&A il Livello 3 copre gia' la maggior parte dei casi, Windows bug -> usa WSL2 o Postgres. 'You run agents offline vs a 5,000+ page brain. Otherwise, no.'

Gbrain: progetto di Garry Tan (CEO di Y Combinator), pensato per accoppiarsi con 'G-stack'. L'autore dichiara esplicitamente di non usarlo quotidianamente ('which is why I don't currently run Gbrain at the moment') pur sperimentandolo con un Hermes Agent, perche' in Claude Code dovrebbe gestire lui stesso i cron. Nessuna schermata di gbrain, G-stack o Hermes Agent appare nel video: solo narrazione audio.

The Build Order — The Four Cs: Context (who you are) -> Connections (your real data) -> Capabilities (skills + agents) -> Cadence (runs on its own). Context+Connections = 'build the second brain'; Capabilities+Cadence = 'make it an operating system'. 'This is the order. But you don't force each step. Usage pulls you to the next C.'

Slide finale 'Find your level: stop at the first yes': re-explaining setup/find by exact word -> L1; 30+ notes keep forgetting -> L2; whiff on notes you KNOW exist -> L3; questions are relationship chains across a cast -> L4; run agents offline vs 5.000+ pages -> L5. First move: L1 folder + CLAUDE.md, L2 ask Claude for an index, L3 Smart Connections, sidecar /memory. 'Climb only for a pain you felt this week. No pain, no climb.'

Concetto centrale ribadito piu' volte: 'your whole project doesn't fit into one level' — diverse cartelle/unita' di business possono stare a livelli diversi contemporaneamente (es. YouTube transcripts come vector DB, context/decisions/projects come markdown puri). Non e' necessario uno stile unico per tutto il second brain.
